audit.whatIsWrong: The page calls the Ntofo Strikes finisher a knock-up in three places ("knock-up with Ntofo", "land the third Ntofo Strikes knock-up", "the third Ntofo cast"). Riot's text: "On hit, grants a stack of Ntofo Strikes. At 2 stacks, K'Sante fires a shockwave that pulls enemies in." It is a PULL, not a knock-up, and it arrives on the second stack, not the third. Separately, Footwork — his 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s dash that also gives a shield — is never mentioned anywhere on the page in either layer.
audit.why: A pull and a knock-up demand opposite responses. Against a knock-up you brace for airborne time; against a pull you have to be outside 450 when the second stack lands, because it drags you into the exact range his whole kit wants. Counting to three instead of two means you commit one Ntofo cast too late — every time. And Footwork is why the poke plan fails at level 3: he has a 10-second dash with a shield attached, so "he has no way to reach you" stops being true the moment he ranks E.
audit.corrected: The finisher named as a pull on the second stack; Footwork named with its 10s cooldown and shield as the reason his gap-close exists at all.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ksante.json (Q Ntofo Strikes: CD 3.5, range 450, 'At 2 stacks, K'Sante fires a shockwave that pulls enemies in'; E Footwork: CD 10/9.5/9/8.5/8, range 525, 'dashes and gains a shield')

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one cooldown appears on the page, though both layers hang the entire plan on "bait the W out before you commit" and "poke when All Out is down".
audit.why: Ntofo Strikes is 3.5 seconds. That single number rewrites the early game the page describes: his stacks are never meaningfully down, so the thing you actually bait is Path Maker at 14/13/12/11/10s, and the thing that decides whether he reaches you is Footwork at 10s. All Out is 120/100/80s — bait it once and you own two minutes. Your own numbers matter too: Thundering Blow is 20s at rank 1, so spending it into a charged Path Maker costs you the next twenty seconds of peel.
audit.corrected: Ntofo 3.5s, Path Maker 14s, Footwork 10s, All Out 120/100/80s and your own 20s Thundering Blow written into the spikes, mid and cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart reads Jayce, Skill, K'Sante, K'Sante, Jayce, K'Sante, K'Sante. It hands K'Sante levels 3 and 4-5 and hands Jayce level 6 — the exact opposite of the prose beneath it. whys[1] calls levels 2-3 "your hardest favour window", whys[3] calls 4-5 a "Skill window — you are ahead", whys[4] says level 6 is "His spike, not yours", and whys[5] calls first item a "Skill check".
audit.why: Five of seven stages disagree with the text under them, and two disagree in the dangerous direction: the chart tells a Jayce to fear his strongest levels and to fight into All Out at 6, which is the one moment the prose says he cannot win.
audit.corrected: Jayce, Jayce, Jayce, Skill, K'Sante, Skill, K'Sante — which is what all seven whys describe.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page attributes a "%HP passive" to Dauntless Instinct in five places and says stacking Armor/MR "feeds the bonus-resist scaling" behind it. Riot's text for Dauntless Instinct is: "K'Sante's Abilities mark targets to take more damage on his next Attack. When All Out, K'Sante deals more damage with all Attacks and Abilities." There is no percent-health component and no resist scaling in it.
audit.why: The reader is given a build rule — starve his resists to starve his damage — that rests on a mechanic Riot's own text does not describe. What the data DOES show is that Path Maker carries true damage, which is the real reason armour is the wrong answer to K'Sante. Pointing the reader at the correct ability keeps the conclusion (don't just stack armour) while fixing the reason.
audit.corrected: The %HP/resist-scaling claim removed; the swap-shred justified by what it actually does, and Path Maker named as the true-damage source that armour does not answer.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are yours, so play forward. Take the Cannon Q and gate-poke his first walk-up to a minion — fire Shock Blast through your Acceleration Gate for the full-range, full-damage accelerated orb, and his only answer is to eat it, since Ntofo Strikes just marks at range and he has no way to reach you. The real prize is the cannon-swap: your first hit after toggling to Hammer form shreds his Armor and MR, which both chunks him now and starves the bonus-resist scaling that fuels his Dauntless Instinct %HP passive. The one trap is Path Maker — if you dump the orb or your Hammer combo into a fully-charged brace, he soaks it through the damage reduction and is unstoppable, so bait the W out before you commit your poke.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are yours, so play forward. Take the Cannon Q and gate-poke his first walk-up to a minion — fire Shock Blast through your Acceleration Gate for the full-range accelerated orb, and until he ranks Footwork he has no way to reach you at all. The real prize is the cannon-swap: your first hit after toggling shreds his Armor and MR, and the swap is a flat 6s so you get it every trade. Two traps. Path Maker charges before it dashes, so an orb dumped into the charge is soaked — bait the 14s W first. And Ntofo Strikes is a 3.5s cooldown: the second stack fires a shockwave that PULLS you in, so the safe distance is outside 450 whenever he has one stack banked.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 you are still clearly ahead — you have both forms and he still lacks the items to fight back, so keep the gate-Q poke war tilting your way and punish every step-up to CS. But Level 6 is where it levels off and tips toward him: your R is not a new tool, it is just the Cannon/Hammer stance swap you already had, while his All Out is a genuine power spike. Once he can brace Path Maker in, land the third Ntofo Strikes knock-up, and turn on his resist-shredding fighter form, he has a real all-in that your poke alone does not stop. Respect that third Ntofo cast pulling you in, and keep Hammer-form Thundering Blow ready to knock him out of the Path Maker charge — but never waste it into the fully-charged unstoppable brace.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 you are still clearly ahead — you have both forms and he still lacks the items to fight back, so keep the gate-Q poke war tilting your way and punish every step-up to CS. Level 6 is where it tips toward him: your R is not a new tool, just the Cannon/Hammer stance swap you already had, while All Out is a genuine 120s spike. Once he can Footwork in on 10s, brace Path Maker through the poke, and pull you with the second Ntofo stack, he has a real all-in that your poke alone does not stop. Thundering Blow is 20s at rank 1 — spend it on the Path Maker charge or on the Footwork entry and mean it, because a wasted knockback leaves you with no peel at all for the next twenty seconds.

notes: MECHANIC ERROR: the page calls the Ntofo Strikes finisher a knock-up in three places and says it lands on the THIRD cast. Riot's text: "On hit, grants a stack of Ntofo Strikes. At 2 stacks, K'Sante fires a shockwave that pulls enemies in." Second stack, and it is a pull — which demands the opposite reaction from a knock-up, because the counterplay is being outside 450 rather than bracing for airborne time. MISSING ENTIRELY: Footwork, his 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s dash-plus-shield, appears nowhere in either layer, so the page's repeated "he has no way to reach you" is only true until he ranks E. Cooldowns added: Ntofo Strikes 3.5s flat, Path Maker 14/13/12/11/10s, Footwork 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s, All Out 120/100/80s, plus your own 6s swap and 20s Thundering Blow. LEVEL CHART: five of seven stages contradicted the whys directly beneath them — the chart gave K'Sante levels 3 and 4-5 (prose: "your hardest favour window", "you are ahead") and gave Jayce level 6 (prose: "His spike, not yours"). Corrected to Jayce/Jayce/Jayce/Skill/K'Sante/Skill/K'Sante. UNVERIFIED, left alone: the page asserts a fully-charged Path Maker is "unstoppable". Riot's text says only that he charges up taking reduced damage, then dashes, knocking back and stunning — unstoppable status is not in the kit data and I could not confirm it, so I removed the phrase only where I was rewriting the sentence anyway and did not restate it. Also flagged: the page credits Dauntless Instinct with a "%HP passive" that scales off his bonus resists, in five places. Riot's text for that passive is only "Abilities mark targets to take more damage on his next Attack" — no percent health, no resist scaling. The true-damage component the reader needs to know about lives on Path Maker instead, and I redirected the claim there. Confidence Medium on that one because I am correcting an absence in Riot's text rather than a contradiction of it.
